utterance:
Samuel, from what you've told me and from examining you, this looks like appendicitis. That's when a small pouch on the bowel, called the appendix, gets inflamed and infected. The pain starting around your belly button and moving to the lower right side, plus feeling sick, not wanting food, a mild fever, and the tenderness I found, all fit with that.

This needs to be seen by the hospital surgical team today. It won't settle with tablets at home, and it can get worse quickly, including the appendix bursting. I'm going to call an ambulance to take you to the emergency department, and I'll phone them so they know you're coming.

Please don't eat or drink anything from now on, in case you need an operation. I'll give you something now for the pain and the nausea. Is there anyone we should call to meet you at the hospital?
reply: My partner, Jess. Can I just go home and get a few things first?

awards.label: Refer to the emergency department today for surgical assessment
Phone the emergency department with a handover

utterance:
Please don't go home first. I know it's inconvenient, but this can worsen within hours, and the bumpy trip and the delay aren't safe. The ambulance will take you straight to hospital. Jess can bring your phone charger, clothes, and anything else you need, and meet you there.

At the hospital they will examine you again, do blood tests and usually a scan, and the surgeons will decide if you need an operation to remove the appendix. Most people with this picture do need surgery, often the same day. You'll be kept from eating and drinking until that's decided.

The paracetamol and the anti-sickness wafer should start helping soon. If the pain suddenly becomes much worse all over your tummy, you vomit repeatedly, you feel faint, or you get a high fever before the ambulance arrives, tell the clinic staff straight away. Do you have any questions?
reply: Okay, I will just wait for the ambulance then. Can I call Jess now?

utterance: Yes, please call Jess now and ask her to meet you at the emergency department, not at home. Stay here until the ambulance arrives, and keep nil by mouth. We'll look after you until they get here.
reply: Yeah, I will call her right now.
